dependent_variable.name: INEW_t
dependent_variable.definition: New investment expenditure: total investment (capital expenditures, acquisitions, and research and development less sales of property, plant, and equipment) less depreciation and amortization; scaled by average total assets.
dependent_variable.formula: INEW_t = (CAPEX_t + Acquisitions_t + RD_t − SalePPE_t − DepreciationAndAmortization_t) / average total assets

evidence.quote: ITOTAL is total investment expenditure. It is calculated as research and development expenditure, RD (item 46) plus capital expenditure, CAPEX (item 128) plus acquisition expenditure, Acquisitions (item 129) less cash receipts from sale of property, plant and equipment, SalePPE (item 107)
INEW is the difference between ITOTAL and IMAINTENANCE
IMAINTENANCE is investment expenditure necessary to maintain assets in place. I proxy for this construct using reported depreciation and amortization (item 125)
All investment expenditure variables are scaled by average total assets (item 6)

independent_variables.name: V/P_{t−1}
independent_variables.definition: Prior-year value-to-market measure of growth opportunities: VAIP divided by market value of equity, calculated as Compustat price item 25 multiplied by shares item 199. VAIP uses book equity, operating income after depreciation, dividends, a 12% discount rate, and abnormal-earnings persistence ω=0.62 (the original text labels the parameter x).
independent_variables.formula: V/P_{t−1} = VAIP_{t−1} / (item25 × item199); VAIP = (1−αr)BV + α(1+r)X − αrd; α=ω/(1+r−ω), r=0.12, ω=0.62

evidence.quote: V/P is a measure of growth opportunities. It is calculated as the ratio of the value of the firm (VAIP) and market value of equity

V/P is V_AIP divided by market value of equity, where market value of equity = Compustat item25 * item199 (multiplication, not subtraction). V_AIP = (1-alpha*r)*BV + alpha*(1+r)*X - alpha*r*d; alpha = omega/(1+r-omega), r=0.12, omega=0.62.
BV is the book value of common equity (item 60), d is annual dividends (item 21) and X is operating income after depreciation (item 178)
The displayed Table2 specification uses V/P_(t-1).

independent_variables.name: Leverage_{t−1}
independent_variables.definition: Prior-year book short-term plus long-term debt divided by book total debt plus book equity.
independent_variables.formula: (short-term debt + long-term debt) / (total debt + book equity)

evidence.quote: Leverage is the sum of the book value of short term
and long term debt
